allowed.name: non-local-deps
allowed.comment: stdlib / third-party / cgo edges pass the allowed matrix; core and tools purity is enforced by the forbidden rules below.

forbidden.name: layer-core-outward
forbidden.comment: internal/core may import only internal/core (core -> core only). Invert the dependency behind a core type or move this code out of core.

forbidden.name: layer-app-outward
forbidden.comment: internal/app may import only core/app/infra (app -> core|app|infra). UI and cmd must depend on app, never the reverse.

forbidden.name: layer-infra-outward
forbidden.comment: internal/infra may import only core/infra (infra -> core|infra). Orchestration on top of infra belongs in app.

forbidden.name: layer-ui-outward
forbidden.comment: internal/ui may import core/app/infra/ui only; importing cmd/... or internal/arch is forbidden.

forbidden.name: layer-cmd-outward
forbidden.comment: cmd/ may import the four layers only (cmd -> core|app|infra|ui). Shared cmd helpers belong in internal/.

forbidden.name: app-no-runtime-adapters
forbidden.comment: internal/app reaches a runtime only through the internal/core/backend ports (Backend, MutationModel, the As* capabilities). Importing a concrete adapter hardcodes one runtime back into orchestration. Route the call through an existing capability, or add a port to core/backend and implement it in every adapter; construction belongs to internal/infra/paneruntime. Test files are exempt so app tests may drive a real adapter directly.

forbidden.name: cmd-no-runtime-adapters
forbidden.comment: cmd/fanout composes through internal/infra/paneruntime, the one package that names a concrete runtime adapter. Naming tmuxrun/tmuxbackend/herdrrun here would spread runtime selection across the composition root. Test files are exempt so cmd tests may build a concrete backend as a fake.

forbidden.name: no-backendtest-in-production
forbidden.comment: internal/infra/backendtest is a test-only fake whose mixins satisfy every backend.As* capability probe. Linking it into the shipping binary would let the fake answer real capability probes, and its class-A (AI-review-only) rating rests on the package never reaching production. Import it from _test.go files only.

forbidden.name: infra-no-new-adapter-importers
forbidden.comment: A neutral-named infra package that imports a concrete adapter and re-exports it as backend.Backend would launder the runtime past app-no-runtime-adapters and the vocabulary test (app would import only the neutral name). The packages that may import a backend-shaped adapter (tmuxbackend, herdrrun) are closed: the adapters themselves and paneruntime (the construction point). A new importer must be added here, which is the review gate. The tmuxrun edge has its own rule below because notify legitimately reaches it.

forbidden.name: infra-no-new-tmuxrun-importers
forbidden.comment: Same laundering guard for the low-level tmuxrun edge. Beyond the adapters and paneruntime, the only reviewed importer is notify's notification sink (notify.go sends display-message to a recorded tmux target); pinning that single file keeps a new backend.Backend-returning helper elsewhere in notify from smuggling a runtime past the app rules.

forbidden.name: meta-no-module-imports
forbidden.comment: internal/arch is the test-only meta package and imports no module-internal packages, so the layer guard cannot depend on what it guards.

forbidden.name: core-purity-stdlib
forbidden.comment: core stdlib purity: no process/network/filesystem/database access from internal/core. The denylist is exact-match on purpose - pure-computation packages under the same trees (net/url, net/netip) stay allowed.

forbidden.name: core-purity-stdlib-agent
forbidden.comment: internal/core/agent is exempt for os and os/exec only (agent CLI validation for live mode); the rest of the core denylist still applies.

forbidden.name: core-purity-stdlib-planspec
forbidden.comment: internal/core/planspec is exempt for os only (spec loading); the rest of the core denylist still applies.

forbidden.name: core-no-third-party
forbidden.comment: core bans third-party modules (and cgo) wholesale, so wrappers cannot smuggle IO into the pure layer.

forbidden.name: tools-stdlib-only
forbidden.comment: tools/ is stdlib-only: no module-internal packages and no third-party modules, so repo meta-tools stay physically separate from product code.

forbidden.name: no-import-cmd
forbidden.comment: importing cmd/... is forbidden everywhere: cmd/fanout is the composition root and shared helpers belong in internal/.

forbidden.name: package-main-location
forbidden.comment: package main is only allowed under cmd/fanout (the one product composition root) or a tools/<tool>/ subdirectory; a bare tools/*.go file is not a valid tool.

forbidden.name: no-bare-tree-root-files
forbidden.comment: no *.go files directly under cmd/, tools/, or a layer root (internal/core|app|infra|ui): every package lives in its own subdirectory, so shared cmd helpers cannot ship outside internal/ and no package can sit at a layer root.

forbidden.name: no-go-files-outside-trees
forbidden.comment: Go code lives only under internal/, cmd/, and tools/: a new Go tree anywhere else (pkg/, examples/, web/, the repo root) would sit outside the layer rules, so it is rejected outright regardless of its imports (fail-closed project shape).
